questions.summary: The smallest step the scale builds on.

options.why: A 4 px base builds a fine grid, and most steps are multiples of 4.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you want a fine grid.
trade_offs: The scale has more steps to name
options.formula: Multiples of 4 pixels, recorded in the chosen unit.

options.why: An 8 px base keeps the scale short and coarse.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you want fewer space tokens.
options.formula: Multiples of 8 pixels, recorded in the chosen unit.

questions.why_care: Every gap is a multiple of this number, so it sets how fine your layout grid is.

questions.prompt: How does the spacing scale grow?
questions.summary: Linear adds the base. Geometric multiplies it.

options.label: Linear
options.why: Linear space adds the same base amount each step.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if gaps should be predictable.

options.label: Geometric
options.why: Geometric space multiplies the base each step, so large gaps grow fast.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if page gaps should jump in size.

questions.why_care: It decides whether gaps grow in even steps or jump in size as they get larger.
One answer covers type, spacing and radius, and it decides whether layout follows the reader's font size.
